subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: For claude-cli, should OpenClaw support native/Workflow-backed background work with durable survival and delivery, or refuse those unsupported affordances and route longwork to OpenClaw-owned Task Flow/Cron/ACP surfaces?
rationale: Current main only shipped a denial for native background Bash and Monitor; choosing the broader Workflow contract changes runtime policy, user-visible tool availability, and completion-delivery ownership.

options.title: Deny Unsupported Native Longwork
options.body: Extend the shipped deny/refusal posture to remaining claude-cli native/Workflow background affordances and document Task Flow, Cron, ACP, or subagents as the supported longwork path.

options.title: Support Durable Native Longwork
options.body: Design a claude-cli background host with origin snapshots, task records, durable completion delivery, cancellation semantics, and live regression proof.

options.title: Hold For Live Repro
options.body: Keep the tracker open but defer implementation until a maintainer reproduces the exact current Workflow-backed failure on v2026.6.11 or main.

recommendation.title: Deny Unsupported Native Longwork
recommendation.body: Extend the shipped deny/refusal posture to remaining claude-cli native/Workflow background affordances and document Task Flow, Cron, ACP, or subagents as the supported longwork path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the claude-cli live-session runtime introduced in this area.
